setup_summary.text: Q3 2026 revenue was $9.45B, up 5.8% year on year and about 5% sequentially. Net income attributable to SLB was $735M and GAAP diluted EPS was $0.49 (vs $0.50). EPS excluding charges and credits was $0.64, up $0.09 sequentially and down $0.05 year on year. The $187M non-cash pension settlement ($0.12) and $0.03 of ChampionX integration costs sit in the GAAP number.

The quarter was a Middle East recovery story. Middle East revenue was $1.9B, up 13% sequentially despite late-quarter disruptions, yet nine-month Middle East revenue is still down 16% ($1.1B) year on year. Pretax segment margin rose 104 bps sequentially, with expansion in all four divisions. Adjusted EBITDA margin was 21.9% (+71 bps).

Q4 guidance is revenue of about $10B (+5% to +7% sequentially) with Middle East revenue held flat at about $1.9B. Adjusted EBITDA margin is guided to expand 100–150 bps from 21.9%. Core divisions are guided up low single digits, with Production Systems up high single digits. Management says Q4 assumes no escalation of the conflict.

Consensus for fiscal Q4 2026 (report due 2027-01-21 after the close) is revenue of $10.01B and EPS of $0.75. Revenue consensus sits on the guided ~$10B. The EPS figure needs a $0.11 step-up from Q3's $0.64 ex-charges. The headline +36% EPS growth compares against $0.55, Q4 2025 GAAP EPS, which carried $561M of charges; consensus is probably on an ex-charges basis, so that growth rate is not like-for-like.

My arithmetic on the guide: 21.9% EBITDA margin on $9.45B is about $2.07B. A 22.9–23.4% margin on about $10B is about $2.29–2.34B, or roughly $220–270M more EBITDA. After tax and over about 1.5B diluted shares, that is about $0.12–0.14 of EPS before any D&A or interest drift. That is consistent with, and slightly above, the $0.75 consensus step-up if guidance is hit.

Free cash flow was $828M in Q3 and company-defined 9M free cash flow was $1.52B (vs $1.83B). Working capital absorbed $1.55B in the nine months, and net debt rose to $9.25B from $7.42B at year-end. Management said that, consistent with its historical pattern, it expects a meaningful Q4 free cash flow step-up from lower inventory after year-end product sales and higher collections, with the size depending on collection timing in certain countries. Q4 2025 free cash flow was about $2.29B (FY $4.115B less 9M $1.826B).

Capital allocation is under more pressure after the Kelvion deal (about $3.4B cash plus about $0.7B assumed debt, closing H1 2027). Net debt is already $9.2B. The year's buyback plan of about $2.4B (9M: $1.755B) and capital investment of about $2.5B are unchanged.
The stock has averaged a ±4.1% closing move over the last 8 reports. No options-implied move is available yet.

since_filing.text: Oil prices have been drifting lower since Oct 29 as renewed US/Israel/Iran diplomacy eased Middle East supply concerns. Prices remain high versus last year (Q3 Brent about $96 vs $69), but Q3 WTI was already about 9% below Q2. Peace would be an activity catalyst in the Middle East, but a lower oil price is a headwind to the broader upcycle narrative.

Baker Hughes (10-Q Oct 28) expects Middle East upstream spending to decline this year and global upstream spending to be broadly flat year on year, with improvement into 2027 absent an oil price decline or higher tensions. It also flagged Strait of Hormuz risk to project timing. This supports SLB's 2027 narrative but argues against a sharp Q4 rebound.

Halliburton's Q3 read-across is mixed. Latin America was +13% and Europe/Africa/CIS +23% year on year, Middle East/Asia was flat, and HAL cites persistent inflation in logistics, chemicals and cement. A summary reports HAL North America revenue down 9% year on year while North America rigs averaged 794 vs 718. That is a pricing/share warning for SLB's North America strength (+24% year on year in Q3, helped by ChampionX).

Sell-side moves in the last two weeks: UBS cut its target to $70 (Buy), Citi to $62 (Buy), Evercore raised to $66, and Freedom Broker upgraded to Hold with a $48 target. Argus reiterated Buy with the stock at about $54.14. SLB traded roughly flat around Oct 29–30 while Baker Hughes fell about 6% on a profit decline despite a beat.

Contradiction between filings and outlook: the 10-K (Jan 23, 2026) expected Middle East rig activity to rise in 2026. The 10-Q (Oct 28, 2026) shows Middle East revenue down 16% ($1.1B) over nine months, and the Q3 call (date not stated) guides Q4 Middle East revenue to about 83% of Q4 2025. The newer 10-Q and call reflect the conflict. The 10-Q also says there are no material changes to the 10-K risk factors, despite attributing the nine-month decline to the conflict.

key_debates.question: Can the Middle East hold at about $1.9B in Q4, and what does a resolution unlock?

bull.text: Q3 Middle East revenue grew 13% despite late-quarter disruptions, the Aramco integrated awards (450+ wells) are committed and mobilising in Q4, and SLB kept resources in place, so a rebound brings strong operating leverage.

bear.text: Activity adjustments were made at the end of Q3 and the Q4 guide assumes current disruption with no escalation. Peers also point to Middle East inflation and an uncertain, partial recovery (HAL) and a Middle East spending decline this year (BKR).

key_debates.what_settles_it: The Q4 Middle East revenue figure versus $1.9B, the Q1 2027 Middle East commentary, and any ceasefire or escalation headlines before Jan 21.

key_debates.question: Is the Q4 EPS bar of $0.75 (vs $0.64 in Q3) conservative or demanding?

bull.text: Guided revenue of about $10B and a 100–150 bps EBITDA margin expansion imply roughly $220–270M more EBITDA, enough to cover the $0.11 step-up. Year-end digital exploration and product sales are seasonally high-margin.

bear.text: The margin guide leans on Digital exploration timing and Middle East leverage. Inflation, pricing pressure on large tenders and Data Center Solutions ramp costs (not accretive to margin) dilute the gain. The tax rate also needs to normalise from 23%.

key_debates.what_settles_it: The reported Q4 adjusted EBITDA margin versus the 22.9–23.4% implied range, and the Digital and Production Systems revenue prints.

key_debates.question: Does the international upcycle hold if oil moderates and peace arrives?

bull.text: Management says the upcycle has long-cycle (deepwater FIDs +30%, exploration) and short-cycle (production recovery) legs, driven by depleted inventories and energy security, and expects mid-single-digit 2027 market growth even with a flat Middle East.

bear.text: Baker Hughes sees upstream spending broadly flat this year with customers disciplined, and Halliburton's North America revenue fell while rigs rose. Oil has started to fall on peace hopes.

key_debates.what_settles_it: The January 2027 outlook (SLB 2027 margins and regional detail), customer capex budgets, and the Brent trajectory.

key_debates.question: Do Data Center Solutions and Kelvion add value or strain the balance sheet and margins?

bull.text: Data Center Solutions grew 23% sequentially, is on track for a $1B run rate by end-2026 and $2B in 2027, and Kelvion adds thermal management content per gigawatt.

bear.text: Growth is dilutive to company margin and All Other pretax income fell on ramp-up costs. Kelvion adds about $4.1B of cash and debt exposure on top of $9.2B net debt, while buybacks (about $2.4B) and capex (about $2.5B) continue.

key_debates.what_settles_it: Q4 free cash flow and year-end net debt, Kelvion financing and leverage commentary, and All Other margin trends.

scenarios.name: base

description.text: Revenue lands near the guided $10B (+5–7% sequentially) with Middle East at about $1.9B. Production Systems grows high single digits and Digital has its seasonal uptick. Adjusted EBITDA margin expands 100–150 bps, EPS ex-charges lands about in line with the $0.75 consensus, and free cash flow steps up sharply.

triggers: Production Systems up high single digits

description.text: A Middle East de-escalation lets deferred activity return and revenue reaches the top of the range (about $10.1B or more). Year-end digital and product sales are strong, margin expands at or above 150 bps, Q4 free cash flow beats on collections, and 2027 margin commentary points to operating leverage. Management called a Middle East resolution a powerful catalyst for 2027.

Disruption in the Middle East deepens or the guided flat $1.9B slips, margin expansion lands below 100 bps on mix, inflation and Data Center Solutions ramp costs, and collections slip into 2027 so free cash flow disappoints. Peers show North America pricing and share pressure and a flat upstream spending backdrop, and lower oil adds pressure on sentiment.

claim.text: Middle East conflict and disruption. Nine-month Middle East revenue is down 16%, late-Q3 activity was adjusted, and the Q4 and 2027 outlooks assume no material escalation. The 10-Q reports no change to the 10-K risk factors.

Margin pressure from inflation and pricing. Well Construction margin fell 346 bps year on year partly on pricing headwinds in select markets, management cites cost inflation and pricing pressure on larger tenders, and Halliburton expects inflation to persist.
Q4 free cash flow and working capital. Working capital absorbed $1.55B in nine months, and management said the size of the Q4 free cash flow step-up depends on collection timing in certain countries.
Kelvion acquisition: about $3.4B cash plus about $0.7B assumed debt, requiring regulatory approvals, on top of $9.25B net debt and the ongoing ChampionX integration.
Data Center Solutions growth is dilutive to company margin and carries ramp-up costs that lowered All Other pretax income in Q3.

Oil price and North America demand signals. Oil has slipped on peace hopes since Oct 29, and Halliburton's North America revenue fell about 9% while rigs rose, pointing to pricing or share pressure that could affect SLB's North America momentum.
Portfolio execution: SLB Capturi took a $210M goodwill impairment in Q4 2025 and had a significant project loss.

questions_for_management.question: What was the Middle East exit rate in September and early Q4 relative to the $1.9B guide, and what disruptions led to the late-Q3 activity adjustments?

why.text: The Q4 guide assumes Middle East revenue stays flat sequentially at about $1.9B with no further escalation; management said some activity adjustments were made at the end of Q3, so how firm is that flat assumption?

questions_for_management.question: Can you bridge the 100–150 bps Q4 EBITDA margin expansion between Digital exploration, Production Systems year-end sales, Middle East leverage and Data Center Solutions dilution?

why.text: Q4 consensus EPS is $0.75 versus Q3 EPS excluding charges of $0.64. Management said overall margin also depends on division mix, and that fast-growing Data Center Solutions is not accretive to overall SLB margin.

questions_for_management.question: How large will Q4 free cash flow be, which countries' collections drive the range, and when do receivables ($9.74B) normalise?

why.text: The size of the step-up depends on collection timing, and receivables and inventories rose sharply in 2026.

questions_for_management.question: How will Kelvion be financed, what leverage level do you target, and does it change the 2027 buyback pace?

why.text: Net debt is $9.25B, the deal adds about $4.1B of cash and debt exposure, and 2026 buybacks and capex are running at about $2.4B and $2.5B.

questions_for_management.question: Are you seeing pricing or share pressure in North America land, given Halliburton's North America revenue decline while rigs rose, and how sustainable is the 7% sequential growth beyond ChampionX?

why.text: A peer summary shows North America revenue falling despite higher rig counts, while SLB's North America growth leaned on production-linked ChampionX and artificial lift.

questions_for_management.question: Will Well Construction pricing headwinds persist into 2027, and how much of the 2027 margin recovery depends on the Middle East versus pricing, inflation and mix?

why.text: Well Construction margin compressed 346 bps year on year, partly on pricing in select markets, and management deferred 2027 margin color to January.
